target.value: Various outreach activities across the country

actual.value:
DR Ramasjang at Libraries DR Ramasjang was present at libraries across Denmark. All main libraries received physical and digital activity materials, and 20 libraries gave the campaign extra focus.
An activity book and worksheets were developed to inspire playful learning about Kenya, rainbow colors, and the TV series The Hunt for the Rainbows Colors. Children were encouraged to go on treasure hunts, color rainbows, draw Kenyan animals, and more.
The library initiative connected TV,web elements with DR Marketing and DR Learn/School, all framed in a playful, engaging context.
DR Marketing DR Marketing launched an interactive photo and video activation where children went on a rainbow color photo safari. Campaign period: November 6 to 30, with trailers and spots on Ramasjang and DR TV.
DR Learn / DR School Produced 6 videos with Tiffany and Ahmed from Nairobi and a Kenyan nomadic tribe. They share their homes, toys, families, camels, daily routines, and more. Worksheets and creative tasks were linked to the videos.
Kenyan Games Danish children were encouraged to play Kenyan games like "Rabbit. Shooter. Wall" and "Bwana Simba" and to make a ball from socks. Extra materials were also created: Learn about Kenya at the Library.

title.narrative: Content for reaching the target group (4-8 year)

target.value: A fiction series in 6 episodes of 8-12 minutes and a music video

actual.value: Fulfilled, On Ramasjang, DR's children's universe for 4 to 8-year-olds, B&U produced a six-episode fiction series, each episode lasting 10 minutes, along with a music video. The content was released for streaming as one complete package and broadcast on linear TV starting from November 6, with one episode airing per week.

title.narrative: Content reaching the target group (9-13 year)

target.value: Five Ultra Special programs of 5 minutes each with Jonas Madsen, known from Ultra Nyt

actual.value: Ultra produced five 5 minute programs with Jonas Madsen, known from Ultra Nyt, who set out to experience Kenya firsthand all the way to the extremes. With five main topics one for each program, which reflects the reality that Kenyan children have even though the filming took place in Denmark. In other words, facts about Kenya told through challenges with a wellknown host with glimpses of Kenyan children's life: Living on 6 kroner a day Food eating grasshoppers and other delicious things Hauling water in the desert in a sauna suit Kenya as a running country can Jonas break the marathon record? Kenya's animals can Jonas stop the poachers and save the animals of the savannah?
